subject.title: autoreview: secret-scanner false positives on identifier and member-expression values (e.g. `apiSecret: ctx.cloudinary.apiSecret`)

question: Should this issue require safe handling for all syntactically valid JavaScript and TypeScript identifier/member-expression references, or only narrowly reviewed roots such as those proposed in https://github.com/openclaw/agent-skills/pull/102?
rationale: The broader rule best matches the issue text but carries greater false-negative risk; the narrow allowlist better preserves fail-closed behavior but may leave the original examples unresolved.

options.title: Keep narrow allowlists
options.body: Review the linked PR’s dialect-scoped roots and require focused tests for every issue example intended to be resolved.

options.title: Accept all source references
options.body: Treat every syntactically valid identifier and member expression as safe in verified JavaScript and TypeScript contexts while retaining concrete secret detectors.

options.title: Add a redacting escape hatch
options.body: Keep strict detection but add an explicit configuration path that removes flagged lines from review input instead of aborting the whole bundle.

recommendation.title: Keep narrow allowlists
recommendation.body: Review the linked PR’s dialect-scoped roots and require focused tests for every issue example intended to be resolved.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and repeatedly refined the current parser-backed source-reference security boundary.
